### 🧠 **Free (or Freemium) AI Tools Like superdesign.dev**

These won’t be *exact* clones, but they serve similar purposes — turning text prompts or quick inputs into UI designs or prototypes:

#### 🔹 **Uizard**

AI-powered UI/UX design tool.

You describe your app idea and it creates screens, wireframes, and flows.

Great for quick prototypes from simple text prompts.

Free tier available with basic features. [Uizard](https://uizard.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

#### 🔹 **UXMagic**

Generates **Figma-editable UI designs from text**.

Can turn prompts into responsive app/website screens.

Has free usage options. [UXMagic.ai](https://uxmagic.ai/ai-ui-design-generator?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

#### 🔹 **UX Pilot**

AI UI design generator that outputs screens you can export or edit further.

Free tier to try basic generation. [uxpilot.ai](https://uxpilot.ai/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

#### 🔹 **Banani**

AI copilot for UI design from text prompts.

Makes editable layouts and mockups fast.

Free and easy for beginners. [banani.co](https://www.banani.co/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

#### 🔹 **Visily**

Simple AI-augmented wireframing and UI design with drag-and-drop plus AI assist.

Has a free plan for basic use. [Visily](https://www.visily.ai/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

#### 🔹 **Figma Make (AI UI Generator)**

Built into Figma, lets you **generate UIs using text prompts** directly inside Figma.

Free with a Figma account. [Figma](https://www.figma.com/solutions/ai-ui-generator/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## ChatGPT

Short answer: **Yes, there is a workable way — but not as a true “live sync” yet.**
What *does* work is setting up **Emergent → external UI editor → back to Emergent** using a **design-first or code-first bridge**, so you can update hundreds of pages **in bulk** without burning credits.

Below is the **most practical, low-friction setup** used by teams in exactly your situation 👇

## ⚠️ First: the hard truth (important)

Right now **Emergent does NOT support direct live two-way syncing** with any UI editor (Figma, Webflow, etc.).

So the correct strategy is:

> **Decouple UI from logic → edit UI externally → re-inject UI in controlled batches**

Once you do this, **you stop touching 250 pages one by one**.

# ✅ Best Working Approach (Recommended)

## 🟢 Option 1: **Figma (Free) → Code → Emergent**

This is the **cleanest + cheapest** way.

### How it works (high level)

Extract **UI layer only** from Emergent

Convert screens into **reusable components**

Edit UI in **Figma (free)**

Export updated components

Replace UI layer in Emergent **once per section**, not per page

### Step-by-step (practical)

#### 1️⃣ Identify repeating UI patterns (CRITICAL)

Instead of 250 pages, you probably have:

5–10 layouts

10–20 card types

5–8 form patterns

👉 List them first:

css

Copy code

• Dashboard layout
• Detail page layout
• Listing page layout
• Settings layout
• Auth layout

This alone reduces 250 → ~15 components.

#### 2️⃣ Move UI to Figma (Free plan is enough)

In Figma:

Create **layout frames** for each page type

Create **components** for:

Headers

Sidebars

Cards

Forms

Tables

Now UI changes = **edit component once**

#### 3️⃣ Export UI back as code (NO AI credits used)

Use any of these **free** options:

**Best free tools**

Figma → manual React / HTML conversion

Figma plugins:

“HTML to Figma” (reverse flow)

“Anima” (free tier)

Or even copy layout specs and re-apply once

> ⚠️ Avoid AI exporters if credits are your pain point

#### 4️⃣ Re-inject UI into Emergent (safe method)

Instead of asking the bot to:

> “Fix UI on page X”

You do:

> “Replace Layout A with updated component”

This:

Touches fewer files

Requires fewer tests

Uses **far fewer Emergent credits**

## 🟢 Option 2: **Local Code Editor (VS Code) → Emergent**

If your Emergent project allows export/import or Git sync:

### Stack

VS Code (free)

Any UI library you already use

One **global UI refactor**

### Why this works

You:

Make **mass search-replace**

Change layout tokens

Update spacing/colors globally

Then push **one stable version** back to Emergent.

## 🔴 What will NOT work (saving you time)

❌ Webflow → Emergent (no clean code roundtrip)
❌ Canva → Emergent (visual only, no structure)
❌ “AI UI editors” → Emergent (credits get burned again)

# 💡 Credit-Saving Strategy (Very Important)

Inside Emergent:

Freeze **logic**

Lock **API + state**

Only let bot touch:

Layout files

Style files

Component wrappers

This reduces:

Test loops

Regression checks

Credit drain

# Optical Retail Software: Enhanced Features and Workflow Design

## Eye Examination Module

Modern optometry systems use an **interactive, single-page exam chart** so providers don’t click between screens. For example, OpenEMR’s Eye Exam form presents *all* eye exam fields on one page – no extra clicks or “submit” buttons[open-emr.org](https://www.open-emr.org/wiki/index.php/Eye_Exam#:~:text=The%20Eye%20Form%20is%20one,all%20in%20front%20of%20you) – and it learns each doctor’s workflow over time. Clinicians can document via **text, drawings, or shorthand** notation, and the system auto-saves as you go[open-emr.org](https://www.open-emr.org/wiki/index.php/Eye_Exam#:~:text=And%20how%20can%20a%20provider,Text%2FShorthand%2FDraw%3F%20Yes%2C%20yes%20and%20yes). Best practice is to customize each exam form for the visit type, displaying only relevant fields to minimize clicks[maximeyes.com](https://www.maximeyes.com/blog/top-optometry-ehr-software-must-haves/#:~:text=Efficiency%20decreases%20dramatically%20when%20you,click%20through%20multiple%20irrelevant%20screens). Ideally, the entire exam (vision tests, refraction results, anterior/posterior findings) fits on a single scrollable view[maximeyes.com](https://www.maximeyes.com/blog/top-optometry-ehr-software-must-haves/#:~:text=3,Screen%20to%20Minimize%20Clicks)[open-emr.org](https://www.open-emr.org/wiki/index.php/Eye_Exam#:~:text=The%20Eye%20Form%20is%20one,all%20in%20front%20of%20you). Crucially, every test result should link to the patient’s record: many solutions let you **attach prescriptions, expiry dates, and doctor notes directly to the exam**[workdo.io](https://workdo.io/product/dash-saas-add-ons/optical-eyecare-center-dash-saas-add-on/#:~:text=Efficiently%20record%20and%20track%20patient,information%2C%20expiry%20dates%2C%20and%20notes)[softhealer.com](https://softhealer.com/blog/articals-11/top-must-have-features-in-an-optical-store-management-system-12680#:~:text=1).

*Example of an integrated eye exam and patient-record interface: patient list and “Add Eye Test & Prescription” form in one view[workdo.io](https://workdo.io/product/dash-saas-add-ons/optical-eyecare-center-dash-saas-add-on/#:~:text=Efficiently%20record%20and%20track%20patient,information%2C%20expiry%20dates%2C%20and%20notes).* Such interfaces allow optometrists to see patient histories, record exam data, and schedule follow-ups seamlessly. As one vendor notes, you can *“record detailed eye test results”* and attach them to patient profiles along with prescription details and expiry dates[workdo.io](https://workdo.io/product/dash-saas-add-ons/optical-eyecare-center-dash-saas-add-on/#:~:text=Efficiently%20record%20and%20track%20patient,information%2C%20expiry%20dates%2C%20and%20notes). To improve your module, ensure the exam form (like [32]) is adaptive and “alive” – it should pull forward old data for easy comparison and pre-fill defaults based on past records[open-emr.org](https://www.open-emr.org/wiki/index.php/Eye_Exam#:~:text=to%20eye%20doctors%2C%20this%20is,section%2C%20or%20all%20of%20it). In summary, redesign the eye-testing flow as a unified page with flexible input methods, patient linkage, and minimal clicking[open-emr.org](https://www.open-emr.org/wiki/index.php/Eye_Exam#:~:text=The%20Eye%20Form%20is%20one,all%20in%20front%20of%20you)[maximeyes.com](https://www.maximeyes.com/blog/top-optometry-ehr-software-must-haves/#:~:text=3,Screen%20to%20Minimize%20Clicks).

## Inventory & Product Management

Inventory should update **in real time** and be fully searchable by attributes (brand, style, size, etc.). Every sale or return should *automatically* adjust stock levels to prevent overselling[eyecloudpro.com](https://eyecloudpro.com/blog/optical-retail-inventory-management-software/#:~:text=1.%20Real). Use a robust tagging or categorization system so staff can filter frames and lenses by style, color, brand, material, SKU and more[eyecloudpro.com](https://eyecloudpro.com/blog/optical-retail-inventory-management-software/#:~:text=2,System). For example, software like Eye Cloud Pro highlights “unique tagging and categorization” to make complex filtering and reporting easy[eyecloudpro.com](https://eyecloudpro.com/blog/optical-retail-inventory-management-software/#:~:text=2,System).

Barcode (or QR code) integration is critical. Each frame or box of lenses should carry a scannable code: this enables a **stock count utility** that quickly verifies inventory on the floor. Indeed, OptoSoft’s system advertises *“full control over inventory with barcode/QRCode”* and “quick physical stock verification using [barcode] scanners”[opto-soft.com](https://www.opto-soft.com/#:~:text=%23%20Inventory%20Management%20System%20,IMS). Adding a **stock-take form** (to count physical inventory) and an automatic **reorder notification** can prevent shrinkage or overstock. Other helpful features include batch adjustments and audit trails: for instance, an advanced system provides manual stock-adjustment entries, branch transfers, and a detailed stock ledger[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,ledgers%20with%20detailed%20transactions%20information). In practice, the inventory module should allow importing stock via Excel, handling returns, and syncing with vendors.

The **Product Wizard** (item creation) should be enhanced accordingly. Ensure the wizard captures all product attributes (e.g. frame style, material, brand, SKU, cost, price, dimensions) and even links to supplier catalogs for easy ordering. It can auto-generate or print barcodes during setup[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,management%20for%20better%20transaction%20visibility)[opto-soft.com](https://www.opto-soft.com/#:~:text=%23%20Inventory%20Management%20System%20,IMS). Embedding the wizard within inventory means that once a new eyewear item is added, the system immediately tracks it in stock. Missing tabs (like separate sections for **incoming shipments**, **adjustments**, **barcode printing**, or **stock transfers**) should be added. For example, one top system offers a built-in barcode/QR printer and scan-powered stock count in the inventory menu[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=Complete%20Inventory%20Management)[opto-soft.com](https://www.opto-soft.com/#:~:text=%23%20Inventory%20Management%20System%20,IMS).

## Customer Relationship Management (CRM)

The CRM must cover the **entire customer lifecycle** with personalized engagement tools. Key features include loyalty programs (points, membership tiers, gift vouchers) and flexible discounts or coupon schemes[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,and%20filters%20for%20multiple%20criteria). Automated communication is essential: set up **SMS/WhatsApp/Email notifications** for order status, lens expiration, eye checkup reminders, birthdays/anniversaries, and appointment recalls[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,and%20filters%20for%20multiple%20criteria)[softhealer.com](https://softhealer.com/blog/articals-11/top-must-have-features-in-an-optical-store-management-system-12680#:~:text=An%20essential%20feature%20of%20any,leading%20to%20better%20customer%20retention). For example, an optical CRM might automatically alert a patient when their contact lens supply is about to expire and prompt them to reorder[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,and%20filters%20for%20multiple%20criteria). Bulk messaging or campaign tools should let you filter customers (by prescription, purchase history, geography, etc.) and send targeted promotions or updates.

Your CRM should also be fully integrated with patient records. Every appointment, exam, and purchase should appear in the customer’s profile. This way, opticians can see a patient’s prescription history when prescribing glasses, and sales staff can suggest upsells based on past purchases. One practice-management guide emphasizes that optical CRM systems *“link [inventory] to customer prescriptions”* and track buying patterns to stock the right frames[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=customers%E2%80%99%20prescriptions,style%2C%20color%20and%20size%20assortment). Moreover, include reporting on customer metrics (e.g. visit frequency, CL capture rate) so you can measure retention and campaign effectiveness. In short, enhance CRM by adding loyalty/points, automated reminders, and marketing modules – all tied directly to patient accounts[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,and%20filters%20for%20multiple%20criteria)[softhealer.com](https://softhealer.com/blog/articals-11/top-must-have-features-in-an-optical-store-management-system-12680#:~:text=An%20essential%20feature%20of%20any,leading%20to%20better%20customer%20retention).

## Forms and Workflow Enhancements

Each functional area needs complete forms and logical workflows reflecting optical retail processes. For inventory, add forms for **stock transfers between stores**, **manual adjustments**, and **stock-taking** with barcodes[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=Complete%20Inventory%20Management). For purchasing, include **purchase-order forms**, goods-receipt (“inward”) forms, and return-authorizations. In the sales flow, implement a **sales-order form** that tracks stages (pending, fitting/adjustment, ready, delivered). In fact, leading optical software provides “sale order management with statuses like pending, in process, in fitting, ready to deliver, delivered”[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,lens%20purchase%20lab%20order%20management), so customers and staff always know an order’s status. Also support partial returns or cancellations with corresponding credit notes and updated inventory.

Every screen should guide the user through the next step. Use tabs or wizards to break long processes into clear sub-forms (e.g. “Patient Information → Prescription → Frame Selection → Order” in checkout). Ensure each form is pre-populated when possible: for example, recall the last prescription so it can be pulled forward[open-emr.org](https://www.open-emr.org/wiki/index.php/Eye_Exam#:~:text=to%20eye%20doctors%2C%20this%20is,section%2C%20or%20all%20of%20it). Include common UI conveniences like *Quick Picks* (clickable lists of frequent exam findings) and defaults for normal values[open-emr.org](https://www.open-emr.org/wiki/index.php/Eye_Exam#:~:text=%2A%20TEXT%3A%20fill%20in%20anatomic,the%20form%20with%20default%20values). The goal is a smooth flow: patient intake, exam, eyewear selection, and checkout all map to sequential forms. In summary, audit each module and fill gaps: add the missing data-entry forms and guided steps that optical staff follow (intake, order entry, adjustments, etc.), following best-practice patterns[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,ledgers%20with%20detailed%20transactions%20information)[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,lens%20purchase%20lab%20order%20management).

## Point-of-Sale (POS) Workflow

The POS should be seamless and integrated with both patient records and inventory. Allow **quick entry** of sales items by barcode or product search. Include buttons like “Quick Sale” or “Add New Customer” (as in [29]) to speed checkout. Most importantly, tie each transaction to the patient and prescription: as Eye Cloud Pro notes, a good system *“syncs inventory, sales, and prescription details”* so that each sale is automatically recorded against the right patient record[eyecloudpro.com](https://eyecloudpro.com/blog/optical-retail-inventory-management-software/#:~:text=With%20seamless%20integration%20between%20your,the%20need%20for%20duplicate%20entry). This avoids duplicate data entry and billing errors.

Support all eyewear scenarios at checkout. For example, staff should be able to ring up frame sales, lens upgrades, special coatings, and services (repairs, adjustments, eye exams) in one transaction. The billing engine should automatically allocate charges (frame, lenses, exam fees) to the invoice and update inventory. Also offer multiple payment methods, split payments, gift voucher redemption, etc. If multiple locations or sales channels exist, the POS should work both online and offline, and push updates when reconnected.

Finally, improve the POS’s user experience and device support. A modern solution might be web-based and mobile-friendly, as one vendor points out: *“Web & Mobile POS system … works on mobile browser as well”*[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=Point%20Of%20Sale%20). Consider a tablet-based POS (to save hardware costs) and ensure the workflow flows logically: e.g., after scanning a frame, immediately prompt for lens options or patient selection, rather than jumping to an unrelated screen. In short, streamline the checkout form and navigation, and integrate it tightly with both CRM and inventory for accurate, efficient sales processing[eyecloudpro.com](https://eyecloudpro.com/blog/optical-retail-inventory-management-software/#:~:text=With%20seamless%20integration%20between%20your,the%20need%20for%20duplicate%20entry)[softhealer.com](https://softhealer.com/blog/articals-11/top-must-have-features-in-an-optical-store-management-system-12680#:~:text=Whether%20it%E2%80%99s%20frames%2C%20lenses%2C%20or,time).

## Reporting and Analytics

Add **comprehensive reports** in every module. Sales reports should cover daily/weekly/monthly revenue, number of transactions, and average sale value. Retail KPIs like *“average purchase value”* and *“total sales count”* are key for visual dashboards[databox.com](https://databox.com/retail-kpi-dashboard#:~:text=5)[databox.com](https://databox.com/retail-kpi-dashboard#:~:text=Also%20known%20as%20total%20sales,total%20number%20of%20units%20sold). Inventory reports should track turnover rates, aging stock, and stock valuation. For example, an analytic dashboard might chart average order value (avg. transaction size) and total revenue, as in standard retail KPI dashboards[databox.com](https://databox.com/retail-kpi-dashboard#:~:text=5)[databox.com](https://databox.com/retail-kpi-dashboard#:~:text=Also%20known%20as%20total%20sales,total%20number%20of%20units%20sold).

Include specialized optometry reports too: prescription capture rate, frame-lens mix, conversion of referrals, etc. Provide batch reporting (exportable to Excel/PDF) on customers (visit frequency, sales by customer), products (top-selling frames/lenses[eyecloudpro.com](https://eyecloudpro.com/blog/optical-retail-inventory-management-software/#:~:text=Custom%20reports%20give%20you%20the,by%20product%20line%20or%20supplier)), and financials (profit & loss, tax summaries). Many systems offer *“50+ advanced reports”* out of the box[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,Excel%2C%20CSV%20or%20PDF%20format). Build dashboards or analytics forms for key users: e.g. sales staff may want a graph of their daily sales versus target, while store managers need stock-level heatmaps. Ultimately, these insights help staff make data-driven decisions (restocking popular items, launching promotions, etc.) and spot issues before they hurt profitability[eyecloudpro.com](https://eyecloudpro.com/blog/optical-retail-inventory-management-software/#:~:text=8)[softhealer.com](https://softhealer.com/blog/articals-11/top-must-have-features-in-an-optical-store-management-system-12680#:~:text=A%20comprehensive%20optical%20store%20management,you%20make%20informed%20business%20decisions).

## Dashboard & Role-Based Interfaces

The dashboard should **immediately show tasks, alerts, and KPIs** relevant to each user. Displaying interactive charts and summary cards helps users orient quickly. For example, an optical dashboard might show “Today’s Sales”, “Monthly Customers”, and quick-action buttons (as in the OptoSoft screenshot below[opto-soft.com](https://www.opto-soft.com/#:~:text=%23%20Inventory%20Management%20System%20,IMS)). Equally important are **task reminders** and notifications: one retail task system emphasizes that *“Tasks are featured on the dashboard”* with automated alerts so nothing falls through the cracks[bindy.com](https://bindy.com/products/task-management/#:~:text=ImageNotifications%20and%20reminders). In practice, this could mean showing open orders pending fitting, appointment reminders, or inventory items that need reordering.

*Sample optical retail dashboard: quick links (sales, orders, customers) and KPI tiles (daily sales, receipts, new customers).* Dashboards should be **graphical** and customizable. Plot charts for sales trends, sales vs. target, or inventory heatmaps. For instance, typical retail dashboards include graphs of total sales and average order size[databox.com](https://databox.com/retail-kpi-dashboard#:~:text=5)[databox.com](https://databox.com/retail-kpi-dashboard#:~:text=Also%20known%20as%20total%20sales,total%20number%20of%20units%20sold). Adding gauges or progress bars for sales goals (“$10k of $15k target”) gives staff instant feedback.

Critically, implement **role-based views**. Each staff type should see only their relevant interface and data. For example, an optometrist’s dashboard might list that day’s appointments, pending exams, and patient recall lists. A salesperson would instead see today’s sales numbers, pending orders, and follow-up reminders. A lab/fitting technician might have a list of glasses ready for pickup. Managers see store-wide totals and charts, accountants see outstanding invoices and financial reports, and area managers compare multiple stores. Modern systems support *“role-based user management”* so each view is tailored[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,for%20retail%20chain%20optical%20stores). In summary, build dashboards with dynamic KPIs, tasks, and reminders, and adapt them by role so every team member gets an at-a-glance overview of what matters most to their job[bindy.com](https://bindy.com/products/task-management/#:~:text=ImageNotifications%20and%20reminders)[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,for%20retail%20chain%20optical%20stores).

**Sources:** We researched best practices for optical retail software and practice-management systems. The recommendations above are based on features of leading optical software (e.g. OptoSoft, Eye Cloud Pro, MaximEyes) and general retail/healthcare dashboards[open-emr.org](https://www.open-emr.org/wiki/index.php/Eye_Exam#:~:text=The%20Eye%20Form%20is%20one,all%20in%20front%20of%20you)[workdo.io](https://workdo.io/product/dash-saas-add-ons/optical-eyecare-center-dash-saas-add-on/#:~:text=Efficiently%20record%20and%20track%20patient,information%2C%20expiry%20dates%2C%20and%20notes)[eyecloudpro.com](https://eyecloudpro.com/blog/optical-retail-inventory-management-software/#:~:text=1.%20Real)[opticalsoftware.org](https://www.opticalsoftware.org/features#:~:text=,and%20filters%20for%20multiple%20criteria)[bindy.com](https://bindy.com/products/task-management/#:~:text=ImageNotifications%20and%20reminders), as cited.

Here’s a **current (2026) snapshot** of where ChatGPT sits versus alternatives and where others might help you:

## 🧠 1. **ChatGPT (GPT-4o / GPT-5 when available)** — Best Generalist & Architect Assistant

**Strengths:**

Best at **complex reasoning, conversation chaining, long project planning**

Excellent for **software architecture, SOP modelling, business logic**

Great at **multi-step instructions, strategy, documentation, and explanation**

Works well with **multi-file / repo workflows**

**This is ideal for your role** in planning, aligning intent, and guiding deep logic.

**Weaknesses:**

Sometimes less strong in *IDE-style real-time coding assistance*

Not always the best for **autonomous multi-file edits or agent-style work** (without structured guidance)

## 🧠 2. **Claude (Anthropic)** — Excellent for Large Context & Safer High-Level Work

Anthropic’s Claude models (like Opus & Sonnet) are **notable for handling very large context windows and deep reasoning**, which can be particularly useful for analysis of:

large SOP docs

long policy logic

multi-role and matrixed controls

Claude is built with a “constitutional AI” framework that can be advantageous for *risk-aware decisions* and extensive logic interpretation. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/ai/what-is-claude-everything-you-need-to-know-about-anthropics-ai-powerhouse?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**When Claude might be better for you:**

Analysing **big policy knowledge bases**

Summarising and reasoning about huge unstructured data

Working on multi-hour continuous tasks

**Keep in mind:** Claude is sometimes more conservative or cautious in responses.

## 🧠 3. **AI Coding Assistants** (IDE-Integrated, not Chatbots)

Tools like:

**GitHub Copilot**

**Tabnine**

**Replit AI**

**Cursor**

are specifically built for *coder workflows in your editor* (VS Code, JetBrains, etc.). These provide:

**autocomplete**

**context-aware suggestions**

**debug insights**

**in-IDE code generation**

These are especially good for code quality and efficiency during development, but they are *not replacements* for planning or intent understanding — they assist at a different layer. [DataCamp](https://www.datacamp.com/blog/best-ai-coding-assistants?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Recommended for:**

daily coding productivity

bug fixing

refactoring

tests generation

## 🧠 4. **Agent/Workflow Tools (e.g., Claude Cowork)**

There are tools emerging (e.g., **Claude Cowork**) that allow AI to:

access your local files

run multi-step tasks autonomously

update code while you sleep

They behave more like digital coworkers than simple chatbots. [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/anthropic-claude-cowork-release-ai-vibecoded-2026-1?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Use-case:**

large refactors

bulk code generation

repetitive maintenance tasks

But you must supply extremely clear guardrails — otherwise they *might* take actions you’d rather supervise first.

## 🧠 5. **Copilot-style Agents (IDE + GitHub)**

Tools that integrate AI directly into your coding environment tend to be the best for *hands-on software building*:

**GitHub Copilot** — deep integration with git/IDE workflows, high-quality suggestions. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/computing/artificial-intelligence/best-llms?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Others (Tabnine, Cursor) — alternative models with strengths in completion and refactoring. [DataCamp](https://www.datacamp.com/blog/10-chatgpt-alternatives?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

These **augment the development workflow**, especially once the architecture and intent are defined.

## 🎯 Bottom Line — What’s Best for *Your* Project

| Task Type | Best AI Tool |
| --- | --- |
| **Complex strategy & intent encoding** | **ChatGPT Plus (or higher OpenAI models)** |
| **Deep context reasoning or huge doc analysis** | **Claude Opus/Sonnet** |
| **Real-time coding assistance** | **GitHub Copilot / Tabnine / Cursor** |
| **Autonomous multi-step workflows** | **Agent tools (e.g., Claude Cowork)** |
| **Search & fact enrolment** | Tools like Perplexity (for citation-oriented searching) [Zapier](https://zapier.com/blog/chatgpt-alternatives/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) |

👉 **ChatGPT is by far the best “all-around” AI for your needs** — meaning architectural guidance, planning, deep multi-sheet logic extraction, repo planning, SOP-to-code translation, and structured thought.

But if you want **deep multimodal document digestion**, **very long context handling**, or **IDE-level automation**, it’s worth combining tools.

## 💡 Practical hybrid workflow (recommended)

**Use ChatGPT Plus / Team / Pro** as your central planning & design AI.

**Use GitHub Copilot / Replit AI / Tabnine** inside your IDE for *daily code generation & refactor help*.

**Use Claude (large context)** when you have *gigantic docs or deep reasoning tasks*.

**Use agent-style tools** only with very strict instructions and a controlled environment.

### **A. Sales staff accountable**

Clear ownership

**Cons:**

### **C. Store manager accountable**

**Meaning:**
Manager owns everything that goes wrong.

**Pros:**

Forces managerial discipline

Simple escalation

**Cons:**

Managers become bottlenecks

Poor root-cause visibility

❌ Not scalable.

### **D. Split with reason tagging**

**Meaning:**
Responsibility is assigned based on:

late handover → sales

fitting error → workshop

capacity issue → manager

**Pros:**

Most accurate

Fair incentives

Best analytics

Supports AI insights later

**Cons:**

Slightly more system complexity (which we can handle)

# SYSTEM_INTENT.md

## What this software is
This is a **Retail Operating System for Optical Businesses in India**, built for:
- Better Vision
- WizOpt
- Future brand extensions

It replaces:
- Excel-based operations
- WhatsApp coordination
- Manual SOP enforcement
- Fragmented POS, inventory, HR, and accounting flows

Tablet-first (iPad landscape), then desktop, then mobile.

---

## Primary Goals
- Single source of truth across stores
- Enforce accountability without killing speed
- Prevent revenue leakage, stock loss, and incentive gaming
- Make operations auditable, explainable, and scalable
- Work with Indian GST, multi-entity, multi-state reality

---

## Non-Goals (By Design)
- No AI auto-running ads
- No campaign creation
- No replacing marketing agency
- No staff-facing analytics spam
- This system is **oversight and control**, not execution chaos

---

## Core Design Principles
- Config-driven logic (no hardcoding business rules)
- Role-based enforcement with overrides + audit trails
- Soft enforcement where needed, hard enforcement where critical
- No silent failures
- Everything traceable to a person, role, store, or time

---

## Locked Operational Decisions (DO NOT CHANGE)

### Orders
- Master Order per visit
- Split billing, split delivery, split incentives allowed
- Accessories, frames, lenses can complete at different times

### Payments & Credit
- Incentives earned only after **full payment**
- Credit allowed only for “Trusted Customers”
- Delivery with outstanding = role-based
- Full audit trail mandatory

### Inventory
- Stock digitally assigned to salesperson (strong accountability)
- Daily stock variance → soft warning + mandatory remark
- Non-moving stock tracked separately
- Accessories: saleable tracked, consumables expensed

### Incentives
- Auto-reversed on returns/exchanges
- Role-based caps
- Anti-gaming logic required
- Incentives never paid on undelivered or unpaid orders

### Daily Glass / Lens Orders
- Vendor known upfront
- Vendor delay tracked
- Staff penalized only if follow-up missed
- Glass order fully linked to POS order, workshop, and customer status

### Workshop / Fitting
- Split accountability via reason tagging:
 - Sales → late handover
 - Workshop → fitting error
 - Manager → capacity issues

### Walkouts
- Mandatory reason capture
- Escalation on repetition
- Visibility depth depends on role
- Full historical access for Admin/Superadmin

### Prescription Validity
- Chosen by optometrist per customer/situation
- Logged and auditable

### HR / Exit
- Mandatory stock, cash, order, incentive checks
- Admin override allowed
- Overrides are logged and visible to Superadmin

### Multi-Brand
- Shared customers
- Shared inventory logic
- Separate GST & finance
- Unified Superadmin view

## ✅ STOCK RESPONSIBILITY MODEL — FINAL (LOCKED)

### 🔹 What you want (confirmed)

**Any salesperson can sell any stock in the store**

**But** each salesperson is **accountable only for the stock assigned to them**

Selling ≠ ownership

Accountability ≠ restriction

This is a **responsibility model**, not an access-control model.

## 🧠 HOW THE SYSTEM WILL IMPLEMENT THIS

### 1️⃣ **Store Stock Pool (Operational Freedom)**

All stock belongs to the **store**

Any salesperson can:

scan

sell

bill

transfer to order

✔ No artificial selling restrictions
✔ No “this is not my stock” excuses

### 2️⃣ **Responsibility Assignment (Accountability Layer)**

Separately, the system maintains:

> **Stock Responsibility Ledger**

For each salesperson:

Assigned SKUs (frames, watches, sunglasses, etc.)

Quantity

Assignment date

Last audit date

This is used **only for**:

daily stock count

shrinkage detection

exit audits

incentive penalties (if applicable)

### 3️⃣ **What Happens During Sale**

If Salesperson **A** sells an item that is:

assigned to **Salesperson B**

Then:

Sale is allowed instantly

System logs:

seller = A

responsibility owner = B

B’s assigned stock reduces

A is **not blamed** for missing stock later

This is exactly how real shops work.

### 4️⃣ **Daily Stock Count Logic**

Each salesperson counts **only their assigned stock**

Store manager sees:

per-person variance

store-level variance

Variance handling follows your locked rule:

**Soft warning + mandatory remark**

Escalation only on patterns

### 5️⃣ **Employee Exit Scenario**

Before a salesperson exits:

System enforces:

stock count of their assigned stock

mismatch resolution

Admin override allowed (logged)

No exit without closure.

“Anyone can sell anything so no one is responsible”

Blame-shifting during audits

Stock loss hidden inside store totals

Punishing the wrong employee

This is **enterprise-grade retail logic**, not basic POS logic.

Pressure escalates based on **repeat behavior**, not one-off mistakes.

| Behavior | UI Effect |

| First miss | Subtle badge (grey/blue) |
| Second miss | Yellow highlight |

Staff are **not punished for one bad day**

### How it works

Task created → calm UI

Near deadline → yellow cue

Past deadline → red cue

### Applied to:

Glass order follow-ups

Cash closing

Stock count

Customer delivery commitments

## 🧠 HOW THIS WORKS IN PRACTICE

### 1️⃣ **HQ Catalog Creation**

Catalog Manager creates/edits SKU master:

SKU is the *price authority*

Price locked at SKU level (global)

Images & attributes attached

Product marked **“Ready for Distribution”**

> HQ does *not* print barcodes.

### 2️⃣ **Dispatch from HQ**

Items move to **In Transit (Unbarcoded)** state

Not sellable anywhere

Clean custody chain (HQ → Store)

### 3️⃣ **Store Receipt & Barcode Printing**

Receiving store:

verifies physical item vs SKU details

prints **store barcode** (linked to the global SKU)

Price is **auto-applied from SKU master**

Store **cannot** change price for that SKU

> Result: same SKU, same price, everywhere.

### 4️⃣ **Mistake Handling (Model / Color / Code)**

If store detects a mismatch (e.g., **1234 vs 1236**):

Store staff **cannot fix it silently**

Store Manager must:

raise an **Escalation**

select error type (model / color / description)

optionally add note / photo

System behavior:

SKU flagged

Item blocked from sale

Notification sent to:

Catalog Manager (HQ)

Admin

Superadmin

### 5️⃣ **HQ Correction Flow**

Catalog Manager sees flagged SKU

Allowed actions:

correct SKU master

confirm store is wrong

split SKU if genuinely different product

All edits:

logged

versioned

time-stamped

Once resolved:

Store reprints barcode

Item becomes sellable

**Price lives only at SKU level**

Store barcode ≠ store price authority

silent store-level price drift

audit confusion

## WHY LINE (1D) BARCODE IS THE RIGHT CHOICE

### 1️⃣ **Speed at POS (most important)**

Line barcodes scan **faster** than QR

Less camera focus issues

Works instantly with:

USB scanners

Bluetooth scanners

Low-light counters

In high-volume retail, **milliseconds matter**.

### 2️⃣ **Cheaper & more reliable hardware**

Every basic barcode scanner supports 1D

QR requires:

better camera

better lighting

higher scanner cost

For 6–8 stores × multiple counters → cost adds up

### 3️⃣ **Perfect for SKU-based retail**

Your inventory reality:

Thousands of frames

Mostly **1–2 pcs per SKU**

Global price per SKU

Store-level barcode printing

1D barcode encoding:

objectivec

Copy code

SKU-ID / Item-ID

That’s all you need.

QR adds **no extra value** here.

### 4️⃣ **Thermal printer compatibility**

1D prints:

smaller

sharper

more durable

QR codes on thermal labels:

blur faster

fail more often

need larger label size

For eyewear tags → **1D is superior**.

## WHEN QR MAKES SENSE (NOT NOW)

QR is useful when:

you want to encode **lots of data**

customer scans code on phone

offline info access is needed

Possible **future uses**:

customer scans QR to track order

QR on invoice

QR on warranty card

**Not for inventory scanning at POS.**

# 🏆 RECOMMENDED HOSTING PLATFORMS

## 1️⃣ **AWS (Amazon Web Services)** — Best All-Around

**Why AWS?**

Industry standard

Proven reliability

Rich ecosystem (compute, storage, databases, caching, queues)

Best options for high availability + redundancy

Works well with Emergent + GitHub actions

**Good for:**

Enterprise-grade ERP

Multi-store operations

Analytics & scheduled jobs

Growth to 20+ stores

**Recommended AWS services:**

**Compute:** AWS Lambda (serverless) or EC2/ECS (containers)

**API / Routing:** API Gateway

**Database:** RDS (PostgreSQL/MySQL) + DynamoDB (optional)

**Storage:** S3 (images, uploads)

**Caching:** ElastiCache (Redis)

**Auth:** Cognito (or custom)

**Monitoring:** CloudWatch

**Pros**

Max control

Best performance

Enterprise integrations supported

Strong security

**Cons**

Some learning curve

Needs good DevOps (but tooling exists)

**Ideal if:** You want *full power + no limits* and are comfortable investing in proper DevOps.

## 2️⃣ **Google Cloud Platform (GCP)** — Great for Data & AI Later

**Why GCP?**

Excellent AI/ML integration (for future insights)

Strong analytics stack

Works well with Firebase

**Good for:**

Apps where data insights matter

Easier scaling with App Engine / Cloud Run

**Pros**

Simple serverless options

Good performance

Generous free tier

**Cons**

Slightly smaller ecosystem compared to AWS

Less enterprise tooling (still strong)

**Ideal if:** You plan to use AI reports and data insights at scale.

## 3️⃣ **Microsoft Azure** — Strong for Enterprise + Security

**Why Azure?**

Excellent support for Microsoft stacks

Good for large enterprises

Great IAM and security

**Pros**

Enterprise compliance

Good integration with Excel / Power BI

**Cons**

Slightly higher cost in some cases

**Ideal if:** Your company already uses Microsoft ecosystem (Office 365, Azure AD).

## 4️⃣ **DigitalOcean + Managed Kubernetes (DO App Platform)** — Best for Simplicity

**Why DigitalOcean?**

Easier than AWS/GCP

Predictable pricing

Good docs, fast setup

Recommended:

**App Platform** (PaaS)

**Managed Databases**

**Spaces** (object storage)

**Pros**

Simple developer experience

Predictable cost

Good for small/medium teams

**Cons**

Not as enterprise-rich as AWS

**Ideal if:** You want lower ops overhead with decent power.

## 5️⃣ **Render / Fly.io / Railway** — Easiest Dev Experience

Great for early stages when:

You want to deploy fast

You want auto-deploy from GitHub

You don’t want to manage servers

**Pros**

Very fast setup

Auto SSL

Simple scaling

**Cons**

Not as battle-tested for large enterprise workloads

**Ideal if:** You want **deployment speed first**, and add AWS later.

## 🧠 DATABASE HOSTING

Your ERP needs a solid DB. Here’s how to pick:

| DB Type | Use For |
| --- | --- |
| **PostgreSQL** | Main transactional data (ERP) |
| **MySQL** | Also solid for ERP |
| **Redis** | Cache, sessions, transient state |
| **ElasticSearch** | Search / analytics (optional) |

I recommend starting with **PostgreSQL** (RDS / Cloud SQL / Managed DB) — strong ACID compliance, excellent tooling.

# 1. GITHUB — SOURCE OF TRUTH (HUMANS + MACHINES)

## What GitHub really is for this project

GitHub is:

the **canonical memory**

the **handover mechanism between humans and AIs**

the **rollback + audit system**

the **integration hub** for Emergent + Render

**Nothing exists unless it is in GitHub.**

## How GitHub stores data

Code + text only (no DB data)

History is immutable (commit log = timeline)

Branches allow experimentation without breaking main

**Critical principle for IMS 2.0**

`main` branch = production intent

no direct commits to main

everything merged via PR (even from Emergent)

## Repo structure best practices (for AI + humans)

Why this matters:
AI reads repos **very literally**.

### We will use:

**Monorepo**

Explicit folders

Zero “magic”

Example (simplified):

perl

ims-2.0/
├── SYSTEM_INTENT.md
├── README.md

├── modules/

 ├── render/

This:

reduces Emergent confusion

keeps coins low

avoids spaghetti dependencies

# 2. EMERGENT — AI DEVELOPER (NOT A MAGIC WAND)

## What Emergent actually does

Emergent:

reads your repo

reads SYSTEM_INTENT.md

generates full-stack code

runs tests

previews the app

It **does NOT understand business unless explicitly told**.

That’s why SYSTEM_INTENT.md matters so much.

## How Emergent stores data

Code lives in its internal workspace

Preview runs on ephemeral containers

Nothing persists unless:

pushed to GitHub

or explicitly saved

**Rule:**
If it’s not in GitHub, assume it’s lost.

## Coin / credit usage (VERY IMPORTANT)

Emergent coins are consumed by:

Large prompts

Repeated refactors

Ambiguous instructions

Asking it to “think” instead of “implement”

### How we reduce coin burn

Never ask Emergent “design”

Never ask Emergent “decide”

Only ask Emergent to **implement already-decided things**

Keep tasks small:

“Implement auth module”

not “build the whole system”

**Your SYSTEM_INTENT.md is a coin-saver.**

## How to work with Emergent efficiently

We will follow this pattern:

Push repo + intent to GitHub

Import into Emergent

Give Emergent **one task at a time**

Push result back to GitHub

Repeat

This avoids:

re-reading entire context

hallucinations

wasted coins

## Languages Emergent works best with (REALITY)

Based on usage patterns:

### Backend

**Node.js + TypeScript** ✅ (best)

Python (FastAPI) ✅ (good)

Java / Spring ❌ (heavy, slow)

PHP ❌ (AI struggles at scale)

### Frontend

**React + TypeScript** ✅

Next.js (App Router) ✅

Vue ❌ (less predictable)

### Database

**PostgreSQL** ✅

MySQL ⚠️

Mongo ❌ (bad for accounting)

👉 **Recommendation for IMS 2.0**

TypeScript everywhere

PostgreSQL

Prisma or Drizzle ORM

This:

aligns with Render

aligns with Emergent

aligns with long-term maintainability

# 3. RENDER — PRODUCTION MUSCLE

## What Render actually is

Render is:

a managed cloud platform

CI/CD from GitHub

production hosting

It is **not** a playground like Emergent.

## How Render stores data

App containers are **stateless**

Persistent data must be in:

managed PostgreSQL

external storage (S3-like)

**Golden rule**

> Never store data on the filesystem.

All uploads → cloud storage
All state → database

## Render deployment model

Connect GitHub repo

Choose service:

Web Service (API)

Static Site (frontend)

On every push:

build

deploy

restart

This is why **clean repo structure matters**.

## Limitations of Render (be aware)

Cold starts on free tier

Background jobs need worker services

Long-running jobs must be async

No cron on free tier (paid needed)

We will:

use background workers

keep AI analysis async

move heavy jobs off request thread

# 4. THIRD-PARTY INTEGRATIONS — HOW WE DO IT SAFELY

## Rule #1

**Never hardcode credentials.**

All integrations use:

environment variables

admin-controlled UI settings

secrets stored in Render

## Integration architecture

Each integration:

lives in `/integrations/{name}`

exposes:

`sync()`

`validate()`

`webhook()`

Example:

bash

Copy code

integrations/shopify/
├── client.ts
├── sync.ts
├── webhook.ts

This:

prevents cross-contamination

makes debugging sane

allows turning integrations on/off

## WhatsApp, Shopify, Payments

All async

All retriable

All logged

All idempotent

No WhatsApp spam. 

No double charges. 

No phantom orders.

## How it works (precisely)

### 1️⃣ Previous Patterns (Deterministic + ML)

Historical sales by **store, category, color, price band**

Sell-through speed, ageing, markdown history

What *looked similar* in the past and how it performed

This uses:

statistical features (velocity, decay curves)

similarity matching (embeddings)

store-specific acceptance patterns

➡️ This is **ground truth**, not prediction fantasy.

### 2️⃣ Trends (Time-aware, not guessing)

Month/season effects (festive, wedding, school season)

Local store trends vs cluster trends

Style fatigue detection (same look repeating)

This uses:

time-series analysis

rolling windows (30/60/90 days)

cluster comparisons (Bokaro vs similar towns)

➡️ It answers *“is this style rising, stable, or dying for us?”*

### 3️⃣ Machine Learning (Used Carefully)

ML is used for **classification and ranking**, not prophecy.

Examples:

“This product is **similar to items that underperformed**”

“This SKU fits **Store A better than Store B**”

“Risk of slow movement: Medium–High”

ML models involved:

similarity models (image + metadata)

clustering models (store behavior)

lightweight regressors (sell-through likelihood)

➡️ Output is always **probability + confidence**, never certainty.

## 🧱 STANDARD LAYER MODEL (APPLIES TO ALL FEATURES)

Every feature has **7 layers** (some critical ones have 8).

### Layer 1 — Feature Activation

Global enable / disable

Effective date

Optional expiry date

### Layer 2 — Scope

Stores (single / multiple / all)

Brands (Better Vision / WizOpt / future)

Categories (Frames, Lenses, Watches, etc.)

Transaction types (POS / Transfer / Purchase / Return)

### Layer 3 — Role Access

Which roles are:

subject to the rule

allowed to override

allowed to view violations

Override hierarchy defined here

### Layer 4 — Thresholds & Conditions

Numeric thresholds

Frequency limits

Time windows

Contextual rules (before/after delivery, advance vs full pay)

### Layer 5 — Behaviour on Violation

Selectable actions:

Soft warning

Mandatory reason capture

Approval required

Temporary block

Auto-escalation

### Layer 6 — Escalation Matrix

Who gets notified

After how long

Escalation ladder (Store → Area → Admin → Superadmin)

SLA timers

### Layer 7 — Audit & Intelligence

Logging level

Data retention

Whether it feeds:

AI insights

risk scoring

staff patterns

### (Optional) Layer 8 — Emergency Controls

Temporary suspension

Manual unlock

Delegation authority

Incident tagging

customer

time

# CORE SHIFT (VERY IMPORTANT)

From now on, we do **NOT** think in terms of:

pages

menus

We think in terms of **LAYERS that exist on every screen**.

Every screen in IMS 2.0 is a **stack of layers**, some visible, some implicit.

# THE 7 UNIVERSAL LAYERS (APPLY TO EVERY SCREEN)

Every screen/page in the software is composed of these **7 layers**.
If a feature doesn’t map to one of these, it doesn’t exist.

## 1️⃣ CONTEXT LAYER (WHERE AM I?)

This is always present, often implicit.

Defines:

Store

Brand

Role(s) active

Category scope

Time context

Authority level

### Example

On **POS screen**:

Store: Bokaro

Brand: Better Vision

Active role: Sales + Cashier

Category: Frames + Lenses

Time: Business Day (pre-cash-close)

This context **locks or unlocks behavior** automatically.

No toggles needed.

## 2️⃣ POLICY LAYER (WHAT IS ALLOWED?)

This is the **hidden engine**, but it directly shapes UI behavior.

For every action:

Can it be done?

Is approval needed?

Is reason required?

Is it blocked?

Is it logged?

### Example

On **Discount field**:

Sales staff sees:

max discount = 10%

reason mandatory after 5%

Store manager sees:

max discount = 20%

override button (approval flow)

Admin sees:

full override

emergency unlock option

Same screen. Different behavior.

## 3️⃣ DATA LAYER (WHAT IS SHOWN?)

This decides:

what data appears

how much history is visible

what is masked

what is read-only vs editable

### Example

On **Customer Profile**:

Sales sees:

name, phone, last visit

Store Manager sees:

lifetime value

outstanding balance

Superadmin sees:

discount dependency

credit exposure

AI risk flags

No separate CRM screens needed — **same page, layered depth**.

## 4️⃣ WORKFLOW / STATE LAYER (WHAT STAGE IS THIS IN?)

Every entity has a **state machine**:

Order

Stock

Task

SOP

Return

Vendor issue

The UI **changes based on state**, not user whim.

### Example

Order screen:

State: “Advance Taken”

delivery blocked

workshop pending

reminder visible

State: “Ready for Delivery”

payment check enforced

invoice printable

State: “Delivered”

editing locked

audit-only view

This prevents forgotten steps without nagging.

## 5️⃣ ACCOUNTABILITY LAYER (WHO OWNS THIS?)

This layer answers:

Who is responsible?

Who is accountable?

Who is notified on failure?

### Example

Inventory item:

Assigned to: Salesperson A

Stored at: Store Bokaro

Last moved by: User X

Next audit due: Date Y

When something goes wrong:

system already knows **who to ask**, not “everyone”.

## 6️⃣ INTELLIGENCE LAYER (WHAT DOES THE SYSTEM THINK?)

This is **never dominant**, but always present.

Appears as:

subtle flags

confidence meters

“Why?” buttons

risk indicators

### Example

On inventory list:

🔴 Slow-moving risk

🟡 Style saturation warning

🟢 Healthy velocity

Clicking opens **explanation**, not action.

AI never hijacks the screen.

## 7️⃣ AUDIT & ESCALATION LAYER (WHAT HAPPENS IF THIS GOES WRONG?)

Invisible but critical.

Defines:

logging

escalation timing

SLA

irreversible actions

emergency overrides

### Example

Cash close missed:

Day 1: store manager notified

Day 2: area manager escalated

Day 3: admin flagged

Repeated pattern → AI insight

No manual follow-ups needed.

## Can AI *directly* change UI/UX and code at Superadmin level?

### ❌ **AI should NOT directly push code or UI changes automatically**

That would be:

legally risky

operationally unsafe

impossible to audit

very hard to roll back

dangerous in a regulated retail + finance + medical context

A “self-modifying production system” sounds powerful, but in real businesses it becomes **uncontrollable tech debt**.

So **full autonomous self-editing software = NO**.

## ✅ What IS the correct, enterprise-grade approach (recommended)

You build a **Self-Evolving System**, not a **Self-Editing System**.

That means:

> AI **proposes**, **simulates**, **scores**, and **packages** changes
> Humans **approve**, **schedule**, and **apply** them

This is how large financial / retail / healthcare systems do it.

## ✅ The RIGHT Model: “AI Change Intelligence Layer”

At **Superadmin level**, AI gets a special capability:

### 1. **AI can IDENTIFY the need for change**

Examples:

“This POS step is causing delays in 3 stores”

“This inventory screen causes repeated overrides”

“This SOP is skipped 28% of the time”

“Sales staff are working around this workflow”

These insights come from:

usage telemetry

failure rates

override patterns

time-on-screen data

error clustering

### 2. **AI can PROPOSE changes (never enforce)**

AI generates **Change Proposals**, not code pushes.

Each proposal includes:

what should change

why it should change

expected benefit

affected roles

affected screens

risk level

rollback plan

Example:

> “Propose merging Screen A + Screen B for Sales role
> Estimated impact: −18% billing time
> Risk: Low
> Affected stores: All
> Requires approval: Superadmin”

### 3. **AI can generate IMPLEMENTATION OPTIONS**

For each proposal, AI can output:

UI wireframe variants

workflow diagrams

pseudo-code / patch suggestions

DB migration plans

feature-flag strategies

But **not apply them automatically**.

### 4. **Superadmin controls the execution gate**

At Superadmin Dashboard:

You see:

🔵 Proposal

🟡 Simulation results

🔴 Risk flags

🧪 Sandbox preview

🔁 Rollback option

You choose:

Reject

Park

Approve for sandbox

Approve for next release

Approve for limited rollout (store / role / brand)

### 5. **AI can auto-implement ONLY in safe zones**

There *are* places where AI can directly act:

✅ Allowed autonomous zones:

Dashboard layout tweaks (card order, grouping)

Report queries & visualizations

Insight dashboards

Notification rules

Alert thresholds

Recommendation logic

Non-financial UI copy

Analytics screens

❌ Forbidden autonomous zones:

POS billing logic

Finance / GST

Inventory movement

Prescription handling

Payment flows

Audit / logs

Role permissions

These zones are **hard-coded in SYSTEM_INTENT.md**.

detecting inefficiencies itself

suggesting improvements continuously

making evolution cheaper and faster

But **never bypassing governance**.

| Area Manager | Resolve store-level delays |
| Admin | Policy & reallocation |
| Superadmin | Final authority |

## 4.2 SLA Stages & Escalation

### Stage 1 – Warning

SLA at risk (e.g. 12 hrs left)

Alert:

Store Manager

Marketplace Control Panel

No penalty yet

### Stage 2 – Escalation

SLA breached

Auto actions:

Flag store

Notify Area Manager

Reduce future allocation to that store

Logged in audit

### Stage 3 – Intervention

Repeated breaches

Actions:

Reassign fulfilment store

Temporarily block store from marketplace orders

Admin approval required

### Stage 4 – Strategic Action

Pattern detected

Ask Intelligence generates proposal:

Reduce marketplace exposure

Change courier

Delist category

Superadmin approval needed.

All mapped back to:

# 3️⃣ Marketplace DB Migration Spec

(**Additive, Safe, No Core Table Changes**)

This is how it should be applied in production.

## 3.1 Migration 001 — Marketplaces Core

sql

Copy code

CREATE TABLE marketplaces (
 id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
 name TEXT,
 region TEXT,
 status TEXT,
 created_at TIMESTAMP
);

## 3.2 Migration 002 — Credentials

sql

Copy code

CREATE TABLE marketplace_credentials (
 id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
 marketplace_id UUID REFERENCES marketplaces(id),
 merchant_id TEXT,
 api_key TEXT,
 api_secret TEXT,
 refresh_token TEXT,
 token_expiry TIMESTAMP,
 last_verified_at TIMESTAMP
);

## 3.3 Migration 003 — Product Mapping

sql

Copy code

CREATE TABLE marketplace_product_mapping (
 id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
 product_id UUID,
 marketplace_id UUID,
 marketplace_sku TEXT,
 listing_status TEXT,
 last_synced_at TIMESTAMP
);

## 3.4 Migration 004 — Pricing Rules

sql

Copy code

CREATE TABLE marketplace_pricing_rules (
 id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
 marketplace_id UUID,
 brand_id UUID,
 category_id UUID,
 markup_percent NUMERIC,
 discount_cap NUMERIC,
 min_net_realization NUMERIC
);

## 3.5 Migration 005 — Inventory Allocation

sql

Copy code

CREATE TABLE marketplace_inventory_allocation (
 id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
 marketplace_id UUID,
 product_id UUID,
 allocation_type TEXT,
 allocation_value NUMERIC,
 safety_buffer NUMERIC
);

## 3.6 Migration 006 — Orders

sql

Copy code

CREATE TABLE marketplace_orders (
 id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
 marketplace_id UUID,
 marketplace_order_id TEXT,
 ims_order_id UUID,
 order_status TEXT,
 sla_deadline TIMESTAMP,
 assigned_store_id UUID
);

## 3.7 Migration 007 — Sync Logs

sql

Copy code

CREATE TABLE marketplace_sync_logs (
 id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
 marketplace_id UUID,
 entity_type TEXT,
 entity_id UUID,
 status TEXT,
 error_message TEXT,
 created_at TIMESTAMP
);

## 3.8 Migration 008 — Courier Intelligence

sql

Copy code

CREATE TABLE courier_performance_metrics (
 id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
 courier_name TEXT,
 region TEXT,
 avg_delivery_time NUMERIC,
 rto_rate NUMERIC,
 failure_rate NUMERIC,
 last_updated TIMESTAMP
);

## User

What is SLA

## ChatGPT

**SLA** stands for **Service Level Agreement**.

But in **your system**, SLA is **not a contract term** — it is an **internal control mechanism**.

Let me explain it **practically**, in your context, not textbook style.

## What SLA means in *your* software

An **SLA is a time-bound expectation for a task or process**, after which:

the system **flags**

then **escalates**

then **intervenes**

SLA =

> *“How long something is allowed to take before it becomes a problem.”*

## SLA in real optical-retail terms (examples)

### 1️⃣ Workshop SLA

Lens order placed → expected completion: **3 days**

If not updated by day 3:

status = **Delayed**

store manager notified

If still unresolved:

area manager notified

If pattern repeats:

HQ + AI flags vendor/store

### 2️⃣ Stock Transfer SLA

Store A ships stock → Store B must confirm receipt in **48 hours**

No confirmation:

reminder sent

escalation triggered

accountability logged

### 3️⃣ POS Cash Closing SLA

End-of-day cash closing must be done **same day**

If missed:

system blocks next-day billing (or flags)

admin notified

This is **mandatory SLA**.

### 4️⃣ Marketplace SLA

Amazon order received → must be packed within **X hours**

Courier pickup delayed:

courier SLA breached

shown in Courier Intelligence

affects courier performance score

### 5️⃣ Customer Delivery SLA (Invisible to customer)

Promised delivery: 5 days

Internally tracked:

day 3: OK

day 5: critical

day 6: escalation

Customer never sees internal failure.

## Types of SLA in your system

### 🔹 Hard SLA

Cannot be ignored

Example:

Cash closing

GST lock dates

System blocks action if breached

### 🔹 Soft SLA

Can be delayed but must be acknowledged

Example:

Daily stock count

Workshop update

Escalates gradually

### 🔹 Conditional SLA

Depends on situation

Example:

Lens remake

Vendor delay

Requires reason + approval

## Why SLA is critical for you

Right now:

delays hide in WhatsApp

excuses repeat

no accountability timeline exists

With SLA:

time becomes **measurable**

excuses become **data**

patterns become **intelligence**

This directly solves:

forgotten lens orders

delayed workshops

non-moving stock

“we’ll do it tomorrow” culture

## SLA ≠ punishment

Important:

SLA is **not disciplinary**

SLA is **visibility + control**

punishment only happens if **patterns repeat**

## How SLA integrates with AI (Superadmin only)

AI can:

detect repeated SLA breaches

identify staff/store/vendor patterns

recommend:

process changes

vendor switches

stock redistribution

AI does **not** auto-act.

## One-line summary

SLA is your system’s internal clock.
It ensures nothing silently dies in WhatsApp or memory.

show **SLA escalation matrix**

or show **how SLA appears in dashboards**

## A. CLINICAL (EYE TEST / OPTOMETRY) — DESIGN PRINCIPLES

### **Principle C1 — Clinical Authority Without Anarchy**

Optometrist has **full authority** at the moment of examination

No real-time AI, admin, or system interference

But every decision is **context-captured**, never silent

> Authority is high, silence is zero.

### **Principle C2 — Context Over Rules**

Prescription validity, remarks, exceptions:

must always allow **free-text clinical reasoning**

never force rigid presets

System records *why*, not just *what*

This avoids:

robotic medicine

defensive optometry

### **Principle C3 — Invisible Oversight**

AI flags:

are **never visible** to optometrists

never affect salary, incentives, or UI

Only Admin / Superadmin see:

outlier patterns

deviation from peer norms

> Optometrist should never feel watched.
> Admin should never be blind.

### **Principle C4 — Peer-Relative Intelligence**

Optometrist behavior is compared:

only within **same store or similar workload**

never chain-wide blindly

No raw averages. Only **contextual deviation**.

### **Principle C5 — Clinical ≠ Commercial**

No commercial metrics (conversion, sale value, discounts) 

appear on optometrist dashboards

Optometry dashboards show:

tests done

follow-ups

prescription quality indicators

redo rates (quietly)

This preserves **professional dignity**.

### **Principle C6 — Patient Safety First, Always**

System blocks:

selling lenses without valid prescription

using expired prescription without explicit override

Overrides:

require optometrist explanation

are audit-logged but never punished automatically

### **Result**

Clinical system now scores **9.7+** because:

autonomy is protected

oversight is silent

intelligence is contextual

dignity is preserved

## B. HR / ATTENDANCE / SALARY / INCENTIVES — DESIGN PRINCIPLES

Reduces walkouts

Credit notes

Prevents compliance penalties

Reduces reconciliation chaos

Saves management time

Monitor task completion

Flag weak stores

Coordinate training

Prevents silent failures

Improves consistency

Reduces dependency on you

**Role**

Decision making

AI insights consumption

Vendor negotiations

Expansion planning

You should NOT run daily ops

HQ exists to *free you*, not consume you

Controlled authority

Tasks, SLAs, patterns

HQ escalates decisions

System assumes:

Humans make mistakes

Processes fail

Silence is dangerous

Therefore:

All failures must surface

All failures must have owners

All failures must leave a trail

### Success Definition

HQ is successful when:

Stores operate calmly

Issues are detected early

Superadmin is not firefighting

Expansion does not increase chaos

Emergent is very good at:

Showing “helpful summaries”

Adding “context panels”

Surfacing “related data”

That’s dangerous unless we freeze **data exposure rules**.

## 🔒 Data Visibility Contracts (What This Layer Does)

For **each screen**, we explicitly define:

✅ Data that **may be displayed**

❌ Data that must **never appear**

🟡 Data that may appear **only after drill-down**

🔐 Data that requires **role + reason**

### Examples (Very Real Risk)

**HQ Dashboard**

❌ Must NOT show individual optometrist names by default

❌ Must NOT show staff salary line items

❌ Must NOT show customer phone numbers

✅ May show aggregates, anonymized trends

**Store POS**

❌ Must NOT show cost price

❌ Must NOT show other stores’ stock

❌ Must NOT show HQ comments

✅ May show offer price, MRP, role-allowed discounts

**Inventory Screens**

❌ Must NOT show vendor credit terms to store

❌ Must NOT show audit variance history to sales staff

✅ May show placement location + accountability owner

Without this layer, Emergent might **technically obey permissions** but still leak **sensitive context visually**.

## What This Layer DOES Define (Required)

### 1️⃣ Button Placement Rules

Examples:

**Primary actions** → bottom-right (mobile), right-aligned (tablet/desktop)

**Destructive actions** → never primary, always secondary + confirm

**Approvals** → right side, visually separated

**Navigation buttons** → never mixed with actions

This prevents Emergent from:

Putting “Approve” next to “Edit”

Making destructive actions too easy

### 2️⃣ Layout Logic Rules

Examples:

Dashboards = **cards only**, no tables by default

Tables allowed only after drill-down

Read-only screens must **visually look read-only**

Actions always separated from data

This prevents:

Dashboards becoming Excel sheets

Action leakage in review screens

### 3️⃣ Text / Language Logic

Examples:

No emotional language (“urgent”, “critical”) → use **status-based wording**

No blame language

System speaks in **facts + timestamps**

Overrides always say *why*, not *who*

This prevents:

Staff fear

Misinterpretation

Authority confusion

## What This Layer DOES NOT Do (Important)

❌ No font choices
❌ No color palette decisions
❌ No spacing or pixel rules
❌ No component-level designs

Those come **after skeletons**, not before.

## The Correct Final Layer

### 🔹 **PROCESS & FLOW CONTRACTS**

This layer answers:

> “In what order must things happen, and what is impossible?”

This prevents Emergent from:

Reordering steps “for convenience”

Skipping mandatory stages

Creating shortcut flows you explicitly don’t want

## What This Layer MUST Define (Required)

### 1️⃣ Screen-to-Screen Flow Order

Example (POS):

Customer → Product → Pricing → Discount → Payment → Confirmation
❌ No jumping directly to payment
❌ No skipping pricing validation

Example (Inventory):

Intake → Verify → Accept → Place → Assign
❌ Cannot place before accept
❌ Cannot sell before place

### 2️⃣ Mandatory vs Optional Screens

Example:

Clinical eye test → **mandatory** if prescription missing

Discount approval → **mandatory** if beyond role cap

Notes → optional but encouraged

Emergent must not guess this.

### 3️⃣ Entry & Exit Conditions

Each screen gets:

**Entry condition:** When can user land here?

**Exit condition:** What must be true to leave?

Example:

Cannot exit “Stock Acceptance” unless mismatch resolved or escalated

Cannot exit “Cash Closing” without reconciliation

### 4️⃣ Failure & Recovery Paths

Example:

Payment fails → retry → switch method → escalate

Workshop delay → notify customer → escalate → SLA reset

Audit mismatch → freeze → assign owner → resolve

This is critical. Emergent otherwise invents “happy paths”.

## What This Layer Does NOT Do

❌ No UI placement
❌ No colors
❌ No component structure
❌ No screen mockups

Those belong **after skeleton build**, not before.

Here’s the **clear, no-fluff explanation** of **“AI read-only (Superadmin only)”**, and **why this is the correct decision** for your system.

## What “AI Read-Only” Means (Precisely)

**AI can:**

Analyze data

Detect patterns

Highlight risks

Suggest actions

Simulate outcomes

Answer questions (Ask Intelligence)

**AI CANNOT:**

Execute any action

Change data

Trigger workflows

Approve anything

Notify staff/customers

Modify UI, rules, or logic

Auto-apply discounts, transfers, purchases, or HR actions

👉 **AI never touches the system state.**

## Why Superadmin-Only

### 1️⃣ **Single Source of Authority**

AI insights influence **strategic decisions**:

Inventory buy/transfer

Pricing discipline

Staff performance

Vendor behaviour

Store health

These must stay with **one accountable human** — *you*.

If Admins see AI:

They will **act informally**

Pressure Store Managers

Bypass policy “because AI said so”

This causes **shadow governance**, which kills systems.

### 2️⃣ **Prevents “AI as Boss” Syndrome**

If staff or admins see AI:

They start defending themselves against AI

They game inputs

They hide data

They blame AI for decisions

Keeping it Superadmin-only:

AI is an **advisor**, not a judge

Humans remain responsible

### 3️⃣ **Legal + Compliance Safety**

AI insights may touch:

HR performance

Clinical behaviour

Financial trends

Showing this widely creates:

Legal exposure

HR disputes

Compliance risk

Superadmin-only = **clean legal boundary**.

## How This Is Implemented (Technically)

### 🔒 3-Layer Lock (Not Just UI)

**Capability Gate**

`INTEL_READ` → assigned only to Superadmin

**Backend Enforcement**

AI endpoints reject non-Superadmin tokens

**UI Non-Existence**

AI screens literally do not exist for others

No disabled buttons

No “coming soon”

Admins cannot even tell AI exists.

## What You Can Do With AI (Safely)

As Superadmin, AI helps you:

Spot **stock dump risk**

Identify **non-moving categories**

Detect **discount abuse**

Flag **staff pattern anomalies**

Recommend **which store needs what**

Simulate **“what if I transfer / buy / stop buying”**

Then **YOU decide**:

Create a task

Ask Admin to act

Change policy

Do nothing

AI never skips you.

## Future Flexibility (Without Risk)

Later, if you choose:

Admins may get **Observation-only views**

Still no execution

Still no simulations

Still no authority

This is already architected — no rewrite needed.

## In One Line (Board-Ready)

> “AI in our system is a strategic advisor visible only to the Superadmin.
> It informs decisions but never executes them.”

This keeps the system:

**Powerful**

**Controlled**

**Future-proof**

**Non-dangerous**

Exactly what a Retail Operating System needs.

# Business Truths – IMS 2.0

This document captures real-world truths that the system must respect,
even when they are inconvenient or messy.

Business Truths:
- Customers pay in parts (advance + delivery), not always cleanly
- Staff often operate under pressure and make mistakes
- Inventory is fashion-driven; overstock and non-moving stock are constant risks

- Clinical decisions are situational, not formulaic

- WhatsApp historically filled gaps where systems failed
- Accountability matters more than speed
- Visibility prevents theft more than policing
- SOPs must be enforced gently, not brutally

If a feature conflicts with these truths, the feature must adapt — not the business.

## VALIDATION RULES SUMMARY

| Field | Rule | Error Message |
|-------|------|---------------|
| Axis (Prescription) | Whole number 1-180 | "R Axis must be a whole number and between 1 and 180." |
| Optometrist | Required if "Tested at store" | "Please select the Optometrist!" |
| Sales Person (Order) | Required | "Please select a sales person type" |
| Pincode | Exactly 6 digits | "Valid 6-digit pincode is required" |
| GST Number | 15 characters, API validation | "The Entered GST Number is not valid" |
| PAN Number | 10 chars (AAAAA9999A format) | Auto-extracted from GSTIN |
| B2B Patient | At least one required | "At least one patient detail is required for B2B customers" |
| Mobile Number | 10 digits | Standard validation |
| Email | Valid format | Standard validation |
| Address Line 1 | Required for billing | "Billing Address 1 is required" |
| City | Required | "Billing city is required" |
| State | Required | "Billing state is required" |
| Vendor Location | Required | "Location should be mandatory" |

## UI COMPONENTS & PATTERNS

### Navigation
- Collapsible sidebar with icons
- Expandable menu items with chevron icons
- Active state highlighting
- Scroll support for long menus

### Forms
- Multi-step wizards (Order, Offer)
- Modal dialogs (Patient details, Stock audit)
- Radio button groups
- Checkbox groups
- Dropdown selects with search
- Autocomplete inputs
- Date pickers
- Country code selectors for phone

### Tables
- Sortable columns
- Inline search filters
- Pagination
- Action buttons (View, Edit, Delete, Toggle)
- Status badges

### Feedback
- Toast notifications for success/error
- Inline validation messages
- Loading states
- Empty states ("No data found")

### Layout
- Fixed header with user info
- Fixed sidebar navigation
- Scrollable content area
- Card-based dashboard widgets
- Chart components for reports

---

## COLOR SCHEME (Observed)
- Primary: Blue (#3B82F6)
- Secondary: Gray shades
- Success: Green
- Error: Red
- Warning: Yellow/Orange
- Background: White/Light gray
- Sidebar: Dark (Navy/Black)

- React with hooks
- Material UI (MUI) components
- Tailwind CSS for styling
- Chart.js or similar for graphs
- React Router for navigation
- Form validation library
- Date handling library (date-fns or moment)

Your system is:

Lose context

Simplify logic

## The correct agent architecture (recommended)

### 1️⃣ **MCP (Master Control Plane) – 1 only**

**Responsibilities**

Enforces:

Non-negotiables

Authority boundaries

“AI is read-only”

Reviews & approves anything from sub-agents

👉 MCP **never builds UI directly**

### 2️⃣ **Main Agent – 1**

This is the *executor*.

**Responsibilities**

Builds screens

Wires navigation

Connects DB + APIs

Talks to Emergent canvas

Create **only when needed**, not upfront.

**POS + Pricing Agent**

**Inventory Lifecycle Agent**

**Clinical / Prescription Agent**

**HR / Attendance / Incentives Agent**

**Finance / GST / Ledger Agent**

**Marketplace + Integrations Agent**

**AI / Intelligence Agent** (read-only)

Each sub-agent:

Knows **only its domain**

Cannot override SYSTEM_INTENT

Cannot talk directly to users

Reports to Main Agent → MCP

## 1. SYSTEM PURPOSE

This software is **NOT a POS**.

It is a **Retail Operating System (ROS)** that governs:
- Inventory
- Sales & POS
- Clinical / Optometry
- HR & Attendance
- Payroll & Incentives
- Finance & Accounting
- Tasks & SOPs
- Compliance (GST, Audit)
- Marketplaces
- Intelligence (Read-only AI)

The system replaces:
- WhatsApp workflows
- Excel sheets
- Manual follow-ups
- Memory-based operations
- Fragmented tools

If a process is not implemented in software, **it does not exist**.

---

## 2. CORE PHILOSOPHY

1. Control > Convenience 
2. Explicit authority > implicit assumptions 
3. Visibility > speed 
4. Auditability > shortcuts 
5. Long-term extensibility without breaking current operations 

No silent defaults. 
No hidden automation. 
No AI execution without approval.

---

## 3. ACTORS & ROLE MODEL

A single user may have **multiple roles**.

### Roles
- Superadmin (CEO)
- Admin (HQ Directors)
- Area Manager
- Store Manager
- Optometrist
- Sales Staff
- Cashier
- Workshop / Fitting Staff
- Catalog Manager (HQ)
- Inventory HQ Team
- Accountant / Finance

### Authority Hierarchy
- Superadmin → absolute authority
- Admin → high authority, limited override
- HQ roles → configuration, pricing, catalog
- Store roles → execution
- Sales / Ops → zero configuration rights

Permissions are:
- Role-based
- Scope-based
- Store-based
- Category-based

Never hardcoded.

---

## 4. APPROVAL, ESCALATION & AUDIT

Every critical action must follow one of:
- Auto-approved
- Role-approved
- Escalated
- Hard-blocked

### Mandatory Audit Logging
- Who
- What
- When
- Where
- Previous value
- New value

No destructive action without trace.

---

## 5. NON-NEGOTIABLE BUSINESS LAWS

### Pricing Logic (Global)
- MRP < Offer Price → **BLOCK**
- MRP > Offer Price → No further discounts
- MRP == Offer Price → Role-based discounts allowed
- Gift Cards allowed in all cases
- Overrides only by HQ roles

### Stock Logic
- Barcodes printed at store level
- Stock accepted only after verification
- Mismatch → escalation mandatory
- Location codes embedded in barcode
- Same SKU must have same price across stores

### GST & Compliance
- GST validation via API
- Locked periods for finance
- Only HQ can unlock
- Exportable to Tally

---

## 6. WORKFLOW INVARIANTS

### POS
- Customer → Patient → Prescription → Product → Payment
- Partial payments allowed
- Credit allowed only for approved customers
- Outstanding tracked automatically

### Inventory
- Central cataloging at HQ
- Store-level acceptance
- Transfers tracked with courier + SLA
- Stock audits mandatory

### Clinical
- Prescription validity controlled by optometrist
- Axis validation enforced
- Clinical data immutable after invoice

### HR
- Attendance
- Leaves
- Late marks
- Incentives
- Salary visibility role-based
- Mobile-first

### Tasks & SOPs
- Role-wise checklists
- Priority-based color coding
- Escalation matrix
- Completion tracking

---

## 7. AI GOVERNANCE (READ-ONLY)

AI is:
- Superadmin-only
- Read-only
- Advisory

AI can:
- Analyze
- Recommend
- Flag
- Propose changes

AI cannot:
- Execute
- Modify data
- Change UI
- Change logic
- Override humans

---

## 8. AI CHANGE PROPOSALS

AI outputs must follow:
- Observation
- Pattern detected
- Risk/Opportunity
- Suggested change
- Impact scope
- Rollback plan

Approval required before any action.

---

## 9. FORBIDDEN BEHAVIORS (HARD STOPS)

- No auto-discounts
- No silent stock edits
- No AI execution
- No cross-store pricing drift
- No deletion without audit
- No bypassing approval chains
- No auto-sync without conflict resolution

---

## 10. VERSIONING & EVOLUTION

- Semantic versioning
- Feature flags
- Role-gated rollout
- Store-wise rollout
- Rollback supported

No breaking changes without migration plan.

---

## 11. EMERGENT BUILD RULES

- Follow this file strictly
- Do not invent features
- Do not simplify workflows
- Do not assume defaults
- Ask if unclear

### 2. `order_items`

`mrp`

`offer_price`

`offer_price == mrp` → role-based discounts allowed

### 3. `invoices`

Legal / financial document

**Key fields**

`id`

`invoice_number`

`order_id`

`store_id`

`status` (UNPAID / PARTIAL / PAID)

`invoice_total`

`gst_total`

`round_off`

`locked_period` (true/false)

`created_at`

**Hard Rules**

❌ Invoice cannot exist without order

❌ Cannot edit after period lock

❌ Refunds via separate flow only

### 4. `payments`

All money movements

**Key fields**

`id`

`invoice_id`

`payment_mode` (Cash / UPI / Card / Gift / Bank)

`amount`

`reference_no`

`received_by`

`received_at`

### 5. `pos_audit_log`

Non-negotiable audit trail

**Key fields**

`entity_type` (ORDER / ITEM / INVOICE)

`entity_id`

`action`

`old_value`

`new_value`

`performed_by`

`performed_at`

`reason` (mandatory on overrides)

Same customer

Same products

Same employee

SKU ID

Store ID

Timestamp hash

Incident logged

Task auto-created for Store Manager

## B2. Fake “Stock Not Found” Sale

**Scenario**

Staff sells product without scanning barcode

Claims “barcode damaged”

**System Defence**

Manual entry allowed **only with reason**

Reason mandatory + category selection

Frequency tracked per staff

Threshold breach → escalation

Result: Manual flexibility without loophole

## B3. Partial Billing Theft

**Scenario**

Customer buys Frame + Lens

Staff bills only frame

**System Defence**

Prescription-linked products auto-checked

POS warns:

> “Prescription exists without lens billing”

Requires confirmation with reason

Pattern flagged if repeated

## B4. Gift Card Laundering

**Scenario**

Gift card used to bypass discount rules

**System Defence**

Gift card usage logged separately

Staff gift-card usage ratio tracked

Abnormal usage → AI advisory (Superadmin only)

Gift cards allowed, abuse detected.

## B5. Stock Transfer Manipulation

**Scenario**

Sending store removes tags

Receiving store claims mismatch

**System Defence**

Pre-dispatch photo upload mandatory

Receiver uploads unpacking photo

Image + SKU auto-linked

HQ arbitration workflow triggered

No verbal disputes. Only evidence.

Staff swaps shifts to hide sales behaviour

**System Defence**

Shift changes logged

Sales linked to **actual shift owner**

Shift-change abuse pattern flagged
